newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey criticises Iran for rebel Kurd attacks.
newsitem.headline: Turkey criticises Iran for rebel Kurd attacks.

text.p: Ankara on Tuesday criticised Tehran for failing to prevent infiltrations of separatist Kurds from Iran to Turkey, which have apparently been on the rise recently.

"I told them whatever measures they had taken were not enough and that they must take more," Interior Minister Mehmet Agar said at a news briefing after meeting an Iranian delegation headed by Tehran's director general of national security affairs.
Turkish security officials have increasingly reported rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) attacks originating from Iranian territory against border positions in Turkey.
In a series of clashes in the past month, Turkish troops killed 128 rebel Kurds who had mounted attacks from Iran, the state-run Anatolian news agency said.
This was about equal to the number of rebels killed after striking from northern Iraq -- where the rebels have bases -- in the same period, the agency said.

Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller, in a meeting with her Iranian counterpart Ali Akbar Velayati earlier this week, also warned Iran over PKK activity on its soil and urged it to take effective action, jointly with Turkey if necesary.
Agar said the Iranian delegation had proposed a joint military operation against the PKK rebels trying to cross into Turkey from bases across the border in Iran.
"But this will not be necessary if each country solves the problem at home," Agar said. He did not elaborate.
More than 20,000 people have died in 12 years of fighting between the PKK and the Turkish army.
Turkish officials often blame neighbour Iran for their alleged support of the PKK, but Tehran denies the charges.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said during a visit to Iran last month that Tehran had assured him it was not supporting the separatist group.

Turkey also accuses neighbour Syria of sponsoring the guerrillas and has said it wants to set up a "security zone" just across the border in northern Iraq to stop rebel infiltration from that country.

Agar said Iran had also complained that outlawed Iranian groups were operating from Turkish territory, and that a security committee of officials from both countries would visit the eastern provinces of Agri and Van by Turkey's Iranian border to work on ways of tightening border security on both sides.
